scenes.tts: Add mature nerve growth factor, or N G F, to cultured sympathetic neurons, and they survive. Now add the same protein before an enzyme has trimmed it. In Barbara Hempstead's experiments, those neurons died. How can one factor carry opposite messages? The answer lies in the receptors on the neuron.
scenes.visual: A mature blue factor reaches a neuron and it turns green and survives; the same factor with an orange tail (uncut) reaches it and it turns red and dies; then unlabelled receptor bars with question marks appear on the cell edge.
scenes.caption: Add mature nerve growth factor, or NGF, to cultured sympathetic neurons, and they survive. Now add the same protein before an enzyme has trimmed it. In Barbara Hempstead's experiments, those neurons died. How can one factor carry opposite messages? The answer lies in the receptors on the neuron.

scenes.tts: A neuron reads a neurotrophin through two kinds of receptor. The first kind is the Trk receptors, said track, and there are three of them. Each prefers particular factors, and N G F prefers Track A. The factor is a dimer, and it brings two receptors together. Their kinase domains then phosphorylate each other, and that starts two survival branches.
scenes.visual: Membrane with three teal Trk bars (TrkA, TrkB, TrkC); NGF dimer arrives and two TrkA bars form around it; phosphate badges pass between the kinase feet and two green branches (Ras to ERK, PI3K to Akt) start.
scenes.caption: A neuron reads a neurotrophin through two kinds of receptor. The first kind is the Trk receptors, said "track", and there are three of them. Each prefers particular factors, and NGF prefers TrkA. The factor is a dimer, and it brings two receptors together. Their kinase domains then phosphorylate each other, and that starts two survival branches.

scenes.tts: The second kind, p seventy five, binds all four neurotrophins but has no kinase. It belongs to the tumor necrosis factor receptor family, like the death receptor Fas. Like Fas, it carries a death domain inside the cell. Trk receptors are locks cut for certain keys. P seventy five is a doorbell that any key can ring.
scenes.visual: A violet p75 bar with a doorbell button; four factor chips ring it in turn; its foot has no kinase but a death domain; TNF-receptor family and Fas chips; the Trk bars pulse as locks and the bell rings.

scenes.tts: Like most secreted proteins, N G F is made as a longer chain. The extra stretch at its front is the pro-domain, and the longer chain is called pro N G F. Cells can trim the pro-domain inside. In 2001, Hempstead and colleagues reported that cells also secrete pro N G F uncut. Outside, plasmin and particular matrix metalloproteinases can cut it.
scenes.visual: proNGF (blue dimer with orange pro-domain tails) sits in a cell; a grey 'trimmed inside?' guess is crossed out; proNGF leaves the cell intact; plasmin and MMP chips cut off the orange tails outside, leaving mature NGF.
scenes.caption: Like most secreted proteins, NGF is made as a longer chain. The extra stretch at its front is the pro-domain, and the longer chain is called proNGF. Cells can trim the pro-domain inside. In 2001, Hempstead and colleagues reported that cells also secrete proNGF uncut. Outside, plasmin and particular matrix metalloproteinases can cut it.

scenes.tts: In their experiments, uncut pro N G F bound p seventy five tightly and activated Track A very little. It triggered apoptosis of cultured sympathetic neurons through p seventy five. For this death signal, p seventy five needs a partner, sortilin, which binds the pro-domain. Mature N G F kept the same kind of neuron alive through Track A. Another group found that uncut pro N G F can also keep these neurons alive, more weakly.
scenes.visual: proNGF docks on p75 with sortilin gripping its pro-domain and a red apoptosis chip appears; then the result clears and mature NGF docks on TrkA with a green survives chip.

Another group found that uncut proNGF can also keep these neurons alive, more weakly.

scenes.tts: Three things go a long way toward setting what one neurotrophin does. Was the factor cut, which receptors does the cell make, and how much of each? How much precursor killing adds to the normal deaths of development is less clear. Cut or uncut, and which receptors: together they go a long way toward setting what the factor says.
scenes.visual: Three columns fill in: cut or uncut, which receptors, how much of each; a grey note that the role in normal development is less clear; a gold chip: what the factor says.
